fixes.explanation: We've all had a friend who gets real quiet when things go wrong. But that's not what the text says here. It says, “In all their distress, He too was afflicted…” God didn't stand off to the side. He was in it with them.

The Jordan isn't named in this verse. The question says, “Where is He who brought them through the sea with the shepherds of His flock?” The prayer goes on to say He “…divided the waters before them…” So the sea is the answer.

Mountains do show up in this prayer, but later. In Isaiah 64:1 the prayer wishes that mountains would quake at God's presence. Here the verse asks, “Where is He who brought them through the sea with the shepherds of His flock?” The answer is sea.
That's the one. The prayer says He “…divided the waters before them to gain for Himself everlasting renown…” Renown means a name people know.

Right, it's false. The verse says He led them “…through the depths like a horse in the wilderness, so that they did not stumble?” They did not stumble, so the part about stumbling the whole way doesn't hold.

Yes, Father. “Yet You are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us.” Then it says it again: “You, O LORD, are our Father…” Even with Abraham not knowing them and Israel not acknowledging them, the prayer holds on to that name.

That's right. The prayer says, “For a short while Your people possessed Your holy place, but our enemies have trampled Your sanctuary.” I think this part is a hard thing to say out loud, and the prayer says it anyway.
The prayer doesn't ask that here. Right after saying they sinned, it asks, “How can we be saved if we remain in our sins?” The question is about staying in their sins.
The verse doesn't say that. The prayer says, “Each of us has become like something unclean, and all our righteous acts are like filthy rags…” Filthy rags are the picture it uses, not something clean.
Right, it's false. The prayer says, “…all our righteous acts are like filthy rags…” It also says, “Each of us has become like something unclean…” Those are the pictures it uses, not clean ones.
That's not what the verse says. The prayer says, “…You have hidden Your face from us and delivered us into the hand of our iniquity.” Hidden is the word, not shining.

Yes, potter. The verse says, “…we are the clay, and You are the potter; we are all the work of Your hand.” I'm a stamper, so I know a little about pressing shapes into soft stuff. But a potter's hands shape the whole thing, and that's the picture here.
Farmer isn't in this verse. Here the verse says, “we are the clay, and You are the potter; we are all the work of Your hand.” Clay is shaped by hands. The potter is the answer.
